hook_text: Forget the brackets and your formula claims FORTY-TWO hydrogens.
clip_script: Now the rule this compound exists to teach: when a polyatomic ion takes a subscript, wrap the whole ion in brackets first. Two ammonium ions: open bracket, N H four, close bracket, subscript two. The full formula: N H four, bracketed, twice, S O four. Why are the brackets non-negotiable? Read the disasters without them. N H forty-two S O four claims forty-two hydrogens. The bracket says: this entire team, taken twice. It is the only honest way to multiply a team.
visual_style: Atom teams in matching jerseys being multiplied: with brackets the whole team duplicates cleanly; without them, a horrifying pile of 42 hydrogen atoms floods the screen.
mood: Comedy of errors turning into crisp rule-setting.
pacing: Absurd hook, fast disaster montage, calm authoritative fix.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write all three formulae yourself.
